tests.name: Effective description
tests.reasoning: The description uses 'Use this skill when...' imperative phrasing, focuses on user intents (which images will be deleted, whether it's safe to apply a policy, why an image disappeared), lists explicit trigger contexts (ECS, Batch, Lambda, App Runner, direct pulls), explicitly lists negative cases to exclude, and is concise (a short paragraph).
tests.evidence: Use this skill when a user asks which images a lifecycle policy will delete or expire, whether it is safe to apply or keep a lifecycle policy, whether an image used by ECS, Batch, Lambda, App Runner or direct pulls is at risk of deletion, why an image disappeared from ECR, or to review lifecycle policies across repositories.

tests.name: Verbosity and conciseness
tests.reasoning: The body jumps directly into project-specific conventions (verdict model, tier evidence, check matrix, scope resolution) without explaining general concepts like what ECR or lifecycle policies are. It assumes agent familiarity with AWS APIs and focuses purely on domain-specific procedures.
tests.evidence: Answer one question precisely for an Amazon ECR repository: which images will the lifecycle policy remove at its next evaluation, and is any of them still in use or tagged as a release?

tests.name: Detailed reference materials must not be in body
tests.reasoning: Detailed reference data (API call shapes, error tables, worked simulation examples, full IAM permission tables) is consistently delegated to references/ files and only summarized or pointed to in the body. The body itself contains procedural logic (verdict rules, check list) rather than raw lookup tables.
tests.evidence: Call shapes, fields, pagination, errors and known quirks are in [ecr-api-reference.md](references/ecr-api-reference.md), loaded at Step 1.

tests.name: Reference files must be linked
tests.reasoning: All six reference files are linked via markdown link syntax in the body (report-template.md, permissions.md, verdict-model.md, check-matrix.md, ecr-lifecycle-semantics.md, ecr-api-reference.md).

tests.name: Reference links must specify when to load
tests.reasoning: Each reference link is accompanied by explicit load-timing guidance tied to specific steps or conditions.
tests.evidence: Load at Step 1. ... Load at Step 4, or section 6 at Step 6 when CloudTrail returned events. ... Load on AccessDenied. ... Load when a verdict is contested. ... Both load at Step 9.

tests.name: Reference path format
tests.reasoning: All reference links use relative paths of the form references/<filename>.md with no absolute paths or traversals.

tests.name: Prescription vs description
tests.reasoning: Fragile operations (push correlation rule, verdict precedence, read-only API restrictions) are given exact prescriptive rules, while flexible areas (scope resolution defaults, protective rule suggestions) explain rationale and allow judgment, matching prescriptiveness to fragility well.
tests.evidence: A BatchGetImage... event within 60 seconds of that image's imagePushedAt is part of the push and MUST NOT count as a consumer pull.

tests.name: Defaults, not menus
tests.reasoning: The skill establishes clear defaults (preview over simulation, tier (a) over (b) over (c)) with fallback alternatives explicitly described rather than listing equal options.
tests.evidence: Preview is the source of truth. Try StartLifecyclePolicyPreview on every run. Only when it cannot complete, simulate, labelling every simulated number SIMULATED.

tests.name: Favor procedures over declarations
tests.reasoning: The skill teaches a generalizable procedure (scope resolution, evidence tiering, verdict assignment, checks) applicable to any repository/policy combination rather than a one-off instance-specific task.
tests.evidence: Step 6. Cross reference every expiring image, tier by tier. Match by digest and by every tag (through the tag to digest map).

tests.name: Gotchas section
tests.reasoning: The skill documents numerous non-obvious environment-specific pitfalls throughout (push correlation false positives, lastRecordedPullTime staleness, guardrail cancellation of preview, EKS pod blind spot) functioning as gotchas even without a dedicated heading.
tests.evidence: ECR refreshes it at least once every 24 hours, so a pull in the last day may not show yet; absence is never proof of non use.

tests.name: Templates and outputs missing
tests.reasoning: The skill explicitly provides an output template reference and enforces its use, satisfying the need for structured output.
tests.evidence: The only acceptable output is the report defined in [report-template.md](references/report-template.md).

tests.name: Templates and outputs must not be in body
tests.reasoning: The full report template is stored in references/report-template.md and only referenced/summarized in the body (heading order, row fields), not embedded as a large inline block.
tests.evidence: Render from [report-template.md](references/report-template.md) with its ## headings in order, Scope through Next Steps

tests.name: Validation loops
tests.reasoning: The skill includes explicit self-validation instructions requiring the agent to check its own output for consistency errors before sending.
tests.evidence: Self check before responding. The expiring image count is identical in Scope, Source of Truth, Expiring Images and the Rule by Rule total... Fix the report before sending if any of these fail.
